function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning: The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test? Actually they give sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, and population mean 98.6. They want to compute the p-value? The phrase "零假設檢定的標準差" maybe means "standard deviation for the null hypothesis test"? But they already gave sample std dev. Maybe they want to compute the standard error? Or compute the t-statistic? The question: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" Might be asking to compute the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? Actually "零假設檢定的標準差" could refer to the standard error of the sampling distribution of the mean under null hypothesis. That is SE = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215. But maybe they want to compute the t-statistic: t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / SE = (98.2 - 98.6) / 0.2215 = -0.4 / 0.2215 = -1.805. Then compute p-value. The user might want the p-value. The phrase "以得到人口平均值為98.6" maybe means "to get the population mean of 98.6". So they want to test H0: mu = 98.6 vs Ha: mu != 98.6. So compute p-value. So we should use the function to calculate p-value. Provide the p-value. Let's compute: sample_mean=98.2, population_mean=98.6, sample_std_dev=1.4, sample_size=40. Use two-tailed test. Compute t-statistic: t = (98.2-98.6)/(1.4/sqrt(40)) = -0.4/(1.4/6.3249) = -0.4/(0.2215) = -1.805. df=39. p-value = 2 * (1 - CDF_t(|t|)). We can approximate using t distribution. For df=39, t=1.805. Using t table: For df=40, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is about 2.021. Our t=1.805 < 2.021, so p > 0.05. For alpha=0.10 two-tailed, t critical ~1.684. Our t=1.805 > 1.684, so p < 0.10. So p between 0.05 and 0.10. Let's approximate using t distribution: For df=39, t=1.805, p ≈ 0.08? Let's compute more precisely: Use approximate formula: p = 2 * (1 - T_cdf(1.805,39)). We can approximate using t distribution table: For df=30, t=1.697 gives p=0.10; t=2.042 gives p=0.05. For df=40, t=1.684 gives p=0.10; t=2.021 gives p=0.05. So at t=1.805, p ~ 0.08. So answer: p-value ≈ 0.08. Provide explanation. Also compute standard error. So answer: Standard error = 0.2215, t-statistic = -1.805, p-value ≈ 0.08. Provide steps.
